title: bee test: stop telling the user the boundary doors run the suite
action: Two stale assertions an independent citation audit found in the SOURCE while auditing docs. Both state, in bare present tense, a boundary auto-run that decisions 58ec9664 and 1f534837 retired: no local door runs commands.test any more — each cap records its own proof line, bee close and bee worktree merge check that record and run nothing themselves, and CI runs the declared command on every push. Verified in code by the audit: run_declared_tests has exactly ONE live caller, the bee test verb itself (test_runner.rs:122); both doors call crate::verbs::cells::feature_proof_check (drivers/close.rs:1524, worktree/phases.rs:150). (1) USER-VISIBLE, the important one — test_runner.rs:114-115, the text bee test prints when commands.test is undeclared, says 'tests prove at the boundary: bee close runs it when the feature has no worktree, bee worktree merge runs it when the feature has one' and 'bee cells finish records tests: boundary and does not run it'. Both halves are now false: no door runs it, and finish records a proof line, not the retired tests: boundary enum value. Rewrite both sentences to state the live rule, keeping the surrounding lines and the next: line intact. CHECK FIRST, then act on what you find: the audit flagged this file as possibly a byte-parity port of an older bee.mjs handleTest, so a parity test may pin the exact wording. Search for such a test before editing; if one exists, update it in the same cell and say so on the cap; if none exists, say that too. (2) COMMENT TOMBSTONE — finish_support.rs:36-38 claims 'bee close and bee worktree merge keep running the declared command through their own copies (drivers/close.rs, worktree/phases.rs) — the boundary is now the only place a test process runs locally'. drivers/close.rs:97-108 already records that those copies were deleted. Correct the comment to match.

The comment at finish_support.rs no longer claims the doors keep their own copies of the declared-command run.
If a parity test pins the printed wording, it is updated in the same cell; if none exists, the cap says so explicitly.
The full suite is green — this cell touches shared verb code, so its scope is the whole suite, not one module.
